stated: Reform UK will front-load the Child Benefit system for children aged 1-4 to give parents the choice to spend more time with their children.

source.quote: Choice for Stay-at-Home Mums or Dads The majority of mothers would choose to stay at home more if they could. Front-loading the Child Benefit system for children aged 1-4 would give parents the choice to spend more time with their children.

bearing_set.reason: Front-loading Child Benefit increases disposable income for families with children aged 1–4, directly affecting household finances during a high-cost early-childhood period.
The policy is explicitly designed to make it financially viable for one parent to leave paid employment; this has a non-negligible effect on workforce participation and household earned income.

Ages 1-4 are a critical developmental window; the policy explicitly targets enabling greater parental time with children in this period, and parental engagement in early years has a documented pathway into later educational attainment and the attainment gap.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: an income boost (O2), a labour-market participation disincentive with long-run earnings consequences (O4), and an early-childhood development effect in a critical developmental window (O7). 'Front-load' implies redistribution within existing Child Benefit spend rather than net new spending, so O12 is not clearly triggered; if confirmed as net new cost, O12 would also earn a bearing.
